27b9a80026fea472.title: My Power Tab.
27b9a80026fea472.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for nutritional supply in cases of general weakness (invigoration), weak constitution, physical fatigue, during and after illness, gastrointestinal disturbance, nutritional disturbance, febrile wasting disease, and pregnancy or breastfeeding.
27b9a80026fea472.usage:
Adults and those aged 15 and older: take 2 tablets per dose. Children aged 7 to 14: take 1 tablet per dose. Take 1 to 2 times daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
27b9a80026fea472.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; children under 7 years of age; severe renal failure; hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking: pregnant or breastfeeding women; patients with a thrombotic (blood-clot) tendency.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

When giving to children, do so under the supervision of a guardian.

Do not take together with levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before taking together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhea, constipation, rash, redness, nausea, vomiting, loose stools, or menstrual changes (earlier periods, gradually heavier flow, or prolonged bleeding) occur, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supports recovery from weak constitution and physical fatigue through invigoration and nutritional supply
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Invigoration, weak constitution, physical fatigue, during and after illness, gastrointestinal disturbance, nutritional disturbance, febrile wasting disease, nutritional supply during pregnancy and breastfeeding

284b4ad4aa99265f.title: Maxel D Tab.
284b4ad4aa99265f.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin D during pregnancy and breastfeeding, growth periods, and old age, to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets, and to supply selenium.
284b4ad4aa99265f.usage:
Adults and those aged 8 and older: take 1 tablet per dose, once daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
284b4ad4aa99265f.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; hypercalcemia (excess calcium in the blood); sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause); kidney disease; infants under 12 months of age; kidney stones; hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking: infants under 1 year of age; children who get plenty of sunlight and eat a normal diet; women who are pregnant or may be pregnant; breastfeeding women; premature or young infants; patients with gastrointestinal diseases such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional colitis; patients with cardiac or circulatory function disorders; kidney disorders; hypoproteinemia; patients with kidney stones or a history of them.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

When giving to children, do so under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, or antacids. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dermatitis, odor in sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disorders, indigestion, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, or pulmonary edema occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamin D and selenium and helps prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Vitamin D supply during pregnancy/breastfeeding, growth periods, and old age; poor development of bones and teeth; prevention of rickets; selenium supply

318155c6d375b9a0.title: Shinil Gel Tab.
318155c6d375b9a0.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for hyperacidity, heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach bloating, indigestion from overeating, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and sour belching.
318155c6d375b9a0.usage:
Adults and those aged 15 and older: take 2 tablets per dose, 3 times daily. Children aged 8 to under 15: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times daily. Take between meals and at bedtime.
Allow at least 4 hours between doses.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
318155c6d375b9a0.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients on dialysis; children aged 7 or younger.

Consult a pharmacist before taking: patients with kidney disorders; those taking other medicines; those on a sodium-restricted diet.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

When giving to children, do so under the supervision of a guardian.

Do not take together with tetracycline antibiotics.

If constipation or diarrhea occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Neutralizes stomach acid to relieve hyperacidity, heartburn, and other stomach symptoms
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Hyperacidity, heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach bloating, indigestion from overeating, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, sour belching

367799c299c3d5d8.title: Dongsung Biotin Tab.
367799c299c3d5d8.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for growth disorders of the fingernails, toenails, or hair caused by biotin deficiency.
367799c299c3d5d8.usage:
Adults: take 1 tablet per dose, once daily before a meal.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
367799c299c3d5d8.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; infants under 3 months of age; hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking: pregnant or breastfeeding women.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

Do not take together with raw eggs. Consult a pharmacist before taking together with carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, or antibiotics.

If hives or gastrointestinal disturbance occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies biotin to improve growth disorders of the nails and hair
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Growth disorders of the fingernails, toenails, or hair caused by biotin deficiency

391039070a7b3041.title: Macta Tab.
391039070a7b3041.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to relieve lower back pain, numbness of the hands and feet, neuralgia, and stiffness of the shoulders and neck.
391039070a7b3041.usage:
Adults and those aged 15 and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times daily after meals.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
391039070a7b3041.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; children under 15 years of age.

Consult a pharmacist before taking: pregnant or breastfeeding women; patients with a thrombotic (blood-clot) tendency; patients deficient in folic acid.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

When giving to children, do so under the supervision of a guardian.

Do not take together with levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before taking together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen.

If rash, redness (flushing), itching, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, mouth sores (stomatitis), abdominal bloating, stomach discomfort, loose stools, constipation, diarrhea, or menstrual changes (earlier periods, gradually heavier flow, or prolonged bleeding) occur, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Relieves lower back pain, numbness of the hands and feet, neuralgia, and shoulder and neck stiffness
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Lower back pain, numbness of the hands and feet, neuralgia, relief of shoulder and neck stiffness

404ac4b22ba9297f.title: Power B-Q Tab.
404ac4b22ba9297f.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins B1, B2, B6, C, D, and E during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, reduced strength during and after illness, growth periods, and old age; to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets; to relieve beriberi, eye strain, neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (lower back pain, shoulder stiffness, etc.), angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, and dermatitis; and to supply zinc.
404ac4b22ba9297f.usage:
Adolescents aged 12 and older and adults: take 1 tablet per dose, once daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
404ac4b22ba9297f.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypercalcemia; sarcoidosis; kidney disease; hypersensitivity to this medicine; infants under 12 months of age; kidney stones; hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking: hyperoxaluria; women who are pregnant or may be pregnant; breastfeeding women; premature or young infants; cardiac or circulatory function disorders; kidney disorders; hypoproteinemia; gout; kidney stones; patients deficient in folic acid.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

This medicine may interfere with glucose detection in urine tests and may turn urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test values. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids, or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before taking together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, antialdosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, redness (flushing), abdominal bloating, loose stools, gastrointestinal disorders, indigestion, upper abdominal pain, loss of appetite, low blood pressure, pulmonary edema, or menstrual changes (earlier periods, gradually heavier flow, or prolonged bleeding) occur, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamins B1, B2, B6, C, D, E and zinc; relieves neuralgia, muscle and joint pain and mouth/skin inflammation; helps prevent poor bone and tooth development and rickets
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Vitamin supply during fatigue, pregnancy/breastfeeding, illness recovery, growth, and old age; poor development of bones and teeth; rickets prevention; beriberi; eye strain; neuralgia; muscle pain; joint pain; angular cheilitis; cheilitis; stomatitis; glossitis; eczema; dermatitis; zinc supply

45561d76fcf67c0e.title: Impactamin Signature Tab.

Adults and those aged 8 and older: take 1 tablet per dose, once daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
45561d76fcf67c0e.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypercalcemia (excess calcium in the blood); sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause); kidney disease; hypersensitivity to this medicine; infants under 12 months of age; kidney stones; severe renal failure; hypersensitivity to soybean oil; those with a history of allergies; hypersensitivity to soybeans or peanuts.

Consult a pharmacist before taking: infants under 1 year of age; patients under a doctor's care; children who get plenty of sunlight and eat a normal diet; women who are pregnant or may be pregnant and breastfeeding women; premature or young infants; gastrointestinal diseases such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional colitis; cardiac or circulatory function disorders; kidney disorders; hypoproteinemia; kidney stones; patients with fat metabolism disorders such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, or pancreatitis, patients requiring careful administration of lipid emulsions, or patients at particular risk from fat overload.

4e96f086e3c16590.title: Active Q-Ten Soft Cap.
4e96f086e3c16590.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins A, E, B1, and C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, reduced strength during and after illness, and old age; to relieve dry eyes and night blindness; to relieve pigmentation (freckles and dark spots) caused by sunlight or skin disease; to help prevent gum bleeding and nosebleeds; and to relieve peripheral circulation disorders and, during menopause, shoulder and neck stiffness, numbness of the hands and feet, and cold hands and feet.
4e96f086e3c16590.usage:
Adults and those aged 12 and older: take 1 capsule per dose, once daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
4e96f086e3c16590.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: women within the first 3 months of pregnancy or who may be pregnant (taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A per day may cause congenital malformations); hypersensitivity to this medicine or to soybean oil, soybeans, or peanuts; infants under 12 months of age.

Consult a pharmacist before taking: hyperoxaluria (excess oxalate excreted in the urine); women who are pregnant or may be pregnant; breastfeeding women; premature or young infants; gastrointestinal diseases such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional colitis; cardiac or circulatory function disorders; kidney disorders; hypoproteinemia; gout or kidney stones; patients with fat metabolism disorders such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, or pancreatitis, patients requiring careful administration of lipid emulsions, or patients at particular risk from fat overload; patients with a thrombotic (blood-clot) tendency; those with hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or a history of it.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

When giving to children, do so under the supervision of a guardian. This medicine may interfere with glucose detection in urine tests. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, or antacids. Consult a pharmacist before taking together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, antialdosterone agents, triamterene, or intravenous lipid preparations. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry rough skin, painful joint swelling, stomach discomfort, diarrhea, constipation, rash, redness (flushing), loose stools, mouth sores (stomatitis), dermatitis, odor in sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disorders, indigestion, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, pulmonary edema, or menstrual changes (earlier periods, gradually heavier flow, or prolonged bleeding) occur, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamins A, E, B1, and C and relieves eye, skin, circulation, and menopause-related symptoms
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Vitamin supply during fatigue, pregnancy/breastfeeding, illness recovery, and old age; dry eyes; night blindness; pigmentation (freckles, dark spots); prevention of gum bleeding and nosebleeds; peripheral circulation disorders; menopausal shoulder/neck stiffness, numbness of hands and feet, cold hands and feet
